items.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I learned about jazz in Pittsburgh at The Encore, listening to Harold Betters. [INTERVIEWEE] Right, the loudest trombone player in the world... He had a hit, “Ram-Bunk-Shush.”

ctx.x: That was my education. And a lot of Pittsburgers don’t know anything about, you know, math as far as music and technical things. Erroll Garner couldn’t read a note. None of those people could read. So that’s how we grew up. Well Pittsburgh had that thing happening anyway because of all of the corporate home offices. At that time there was the large home offices for private big businesses like Gulf and Westinghouse’s home office was there, U.S. Steel, Jones & Laughlin, you had Rockwell, you had Heinz. You had 54…
I learned about jazz in Pittsburgh at The Encore, listening to Harold Betters.
Right, the loudest trombone player in the world, if you listen you could hear him. He had a hit, “Ram-Bunk-Shush.” He had that hit, you know?
